subject: microbiology
title: Rickettsia prowazekii, Epidemic Typhus and Scrub Typhus

steps.tx: **Rickettsia prowazekii** is an obligate intracellular gram negative bacterium transmitted by human body lice and causes epidemic typhus. Louse faeces are scratched into skin or mucous membranes rather than inoculated by a bite alone. Crowding, war, displacement and inability to wash or change clothes drive outbreaks. Fever, severe headache, myalgia and a centrifugal rash cause confusion with other febrile exanthems.
steps.say: Epidemic typhus follows body lice and crowding, not simply a tick bite.

vis.alt: Rickettsial disease visual clues including rash and eschar patterns
vis.caption: Rickettsial diseases may show eschars, rashes and vector clues.

steps.tx: Rickettsiae invade **endothelial cells**, multiply intracellularly and spread cell to cell, injuring small vessels throughout the body. Vasculitis explains rash, meningoencephalitis, pneumonitis, myocarditis, acute kidney injury and digital or skin necrosis in severe disease. Rocky Mountain spotted fever demonstrates that capillary leakage and thrombocytopenia can kill before confirmatory antibody tests become positive.
steps.say: Endothelial infection turns rickettsial disease into systemic small vessel vasculitis.

left.title: Pathogenesis
points: Endothelial entry and intracellular replication
Cell injury and increased permeability
Platelet consumption and microthrombi
Perivascular lymphohistiocytic inflammation

right.title: Consequences
points: Petechial or maculopapular rash
Encephalopathy and meningismus
Hypotension and oedema
Gangrene in fulminant disease

steps.tx: **Scrub typhus** is caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi and transmitted by larval trombiculid mites called chiggers. It is a major cause of acute febrile illness across the tsutsugamushi triangle in Asia and the Pacific. An eschar at the bite site, regional lymphadenopathy, fever and rash are important clues, but eschar frequency varies by population and skin pigmentation and absence cannot exclude the diagnosis.
steps.say: Scrub typhus is mite borne Orientia disease; an eschar helps greatly but is not mandatory.

left.title: Exposure pattern
points: Grass, scrub and agricultural work
Rodents and mites maintain transmission cycles
Outdoor sleeping and military field exposure
Seasonal peaks with vegetation and rain

right.title: Clinical clues
points: Eschar often in groin, axilla or waistline
Fever and severe headache
Lymphadenopathy near eschar
Hepatitis, pneumonitis or meningoencephalitis in severe cases

steps.tx: Early rickettsial diagnosis is frequently clinical because **antibodies rise later**. PCR from blood, eschar swab or biopsy can help before seroconversion. Immunofluorescence is a reference serology, while IgM enzyme assays vary in specificity. The Weil Felix test is historically important and still used in some settings, but cross reactivity and poor sensitivity make it unreliable as the sole basis for urgent treatment decisions.
steps.say: Do not wait for rickettsial serology when fever, exposure and rash justify immediate doxycycline.

left.title: Early tests
points: Eschar PCR has high yield in scrub typhus
Buffy coat or whole blood PCR varies by day
Skin biopsy immunohistochemistry in reference centres
Acute serology often negative

right.title: Later tests
points: Paired serology shows fourfold rise
IgM may cross react or persist
Weil Felix uses Proteus OX antigens
Blood cultures are unhelpful for obligate intracellular organisms

steps.tx: **Doxycycline** is the cornerstone treatment for epidemic typhus, spotted fever rickettsioses and scrub typhus, including in young children when the diagnosis is likely because short courses have a favourable safety profile compared with untreated rickettsial mortality. Fever often improves within forty eight hours, but lack of rapid improvement should prompt reconsideration of diagnosis, complications or alternative therapy rather than abandoning the rickettsial hypothesis too early.
steps.say: Doxycycline should not be withheld from a likely rickettsial illness because of age alone.

left.title: Treatment points
points: Start empirically on clinical suspicion
Children with spotted fever should receive doxycycline
Severe disease may need intensive organ support
Azithromycin is used in selected scrub typhus settings

right.title: If fever persists
points: Check adherence and absorption
Seek pneumonia, abscess or another fever cause
Consider doxycycline resistance signals regionally
Use specialist advice for pregnancy and severe disease

steps.tx: **Brill Zinsser disease** is recrudescence of R prowazekii years after primary epidemic typhus, usually milder and without lice initially, but capable of initiating a new epidemic if body lice are present. It illustrates bacterial latency within a recovered human host. Control of epidemic typhus therefore combines antibiotics, delousing, clothing hygiene and social measures that interrupt the human louse human cycle.
steps.say: A remote typhus infection can recrudesce as Brill Zinsser disease and reseed lice borne transmission.
